title: What Claude Code's Leaked Source Code Reveals: 8 Insights for Power Users
summary: Claude Code's source code was inadvertently leaked via an NPM package source map, revealing that it's a full agent runtime — not just a chatbot in your terminal. The creator breaks down 8 practical insights from the leak, covering hidden commands, the memory system, permissions tuning, multi-agent architecture, and a framework for using Claude Code like a top 1% user.

title: Replacing Complex n8n RAG Pipelines with Pinecone's Assistant Node
summary: Pinecone released a free assistant node for n8n that collapses an entire RAG pipeline — chunking, re-ranking, and retrieval optimizations — into a single node. Cole Medin walks through a workflow template that watches a Google Drive folder for files, ingests them into the Pinecone assistant, and answers questions with an RAG agent, replacing what used to be a sprawling multi-node setup.

title: The Axios Supply Chain Attack: How a Single Dependency Hijack Deploys a RAT in 1.1 Seconds
summary: The Axios npm package (100M+ weekly downloads) was hijacked via a compromised maintainer access token. The attacker added a single malicious dependency to package.json that installs a remote access Trojan in 1.1 seconds, then erases all evidence of itself. Affected versions are 1.14.1 and 0.30.4 — and you likely have Axios installed transitively without knowing it.

title: Gemini 3.1 Flash Live: Google's Speech-to-Speech Model for Voice Agents
summary: Google released Gemini 3.1 Flash Live, a speech-to-speech voice model that skips the traditional speech-to-text-to-speech pipeline. It outperforms Gemini 2.5 Flash by ~19% on multi-step function calling, handles noisy environments, and understands vocal context like sarcasm and frustration — relevant for anyone building voice-based customer support or sales agents.

title: Setting Up OpenClaw: AI Agent Gateway on a VPS with Telegram Integration
summary: OpenClaw is an open-source AI agent gateway that connects AI models (OpenAI, Anthropic, local) to messaging channels (Telegram, Discord, Slack) with persistent memory and system-level tool access. This tutorial walks through installing it on a VPS, configuring an agent with Telegram, building quick projects (news dashboard, IT monitoring), and locking down security.

title: Building Voice Agents with Gemini 3.1 Flash Live: Free Playground to Production Demos
summary: Google released Gemini 3.1 Flash Live, a speech-to-speech voice model with vision, tool calling, and low latency. This walkthrough covers using it free in Google AI Studio, customizing agents with system instructions, and building two demo integrations (a product website voice widget and a personal assistant with ClickUp/Calendar tools) using Claude Code — all built in under 30 minutes each.

title: Automating GitHub Issues with Claude Code and Coder Workspaces
summary: Cole Medin demonstrates how to use Coder Workspaces — a free, open-source orchestration layer — to automatically spin up remote Claude Code instances that handle GitHub issues end-to-end, from reading the issue to creating a pull request, without anything running on your local machine.

title: Setting Up Paperclip: Open-Source AI Agent Orchestration with Claude Code
summary: Paperclip is a free, open-source (MIT license) orchestration platform for running multiple AI agents as a virtual company — complete with a dashboard, ticketing system, heartbeats, budgets, and approval workflows. This tutorial walks through setting it up from scratch with Claude Code, creating agents, assigning tasks, installing skills, and managing an autonomous agent organization.

title: Adversarial Dev: Why Pitting Two Coding Agents Against Each Other Produces Far Better Code
summary: Cole Medin argues that sycophancy — AI models agreeing with themselves and the user too readily — is the biggest reliability problem in AI coding today, and it's getting worse as models improve. His proposed solution: a GAN-inspired multi-agent harness where a separate evaluator agent adversarially critiques a generator agent's code, negotiating evaluation contracts and iterating through sprints automatically. He built and open-sourced harnesses for both Claude Code and Codex to prove the approach works.

title: 18 Claude Code Token Management Hacks to Stretch Your Usage 2-5x
summary: Claude Code's token system compounds exponentially per message because it rereads the entire conversation history every turn — 98.5% of tokens in a 100+ message chat were just rereading old history. This video covers 18 hacks organized in three tiers (basic, intermediate, advanced) to dramatically reduce token waste and extend your session life.

title: Build Your Own AI Second Brain with Claude Code and Obsidian
summary: Cole Medin walks through the full architecture of his Claude Code + Obsidian-based AI second brain that he claims saves him 12+ hours per week. Rather than using an off-the-shelf solution like Open Claw, he argues for building your own for security and customization reasons, and provides a GitHub template that generates a phased PRD to guide you through building it.

summary:
Building an agent that can generate an entire interactive course from a PDF/textbook 🤯

The way it works: I have pre-built components (Q&A, drag & match, flowchart, info bubble, ect...) that can be invoked through tool calls.

Here's the full workflow:

1. The agent will first parse the material passed in (can either remain in context if small or be embedded if big)
2. Agent will then decide on a good structure for the lesson (will be given a few good examples for reference)
3. Through tool calling, it will be able to select the right components now that it has a lesson structure. It will also pass in the relevant params to the components (like generated questions or content for a flowchart).
4. The finished lesson gets handed off to a Lesson Reviewer agent for a final check against source material
5. Lesson gets created & is able to be sent to others

This app will be built with open source LLMs from @togethercompute and will be free & open source!

I think this will turn out to be one of my most interesting apps. Let me know if y'all want to see a guide on how I built it as well!
